newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey says credit rating should be based on '97 plan.
newsitem.headline: Turkey says credit rating should be based on '97 plan.

text.p: State Minister Ayfer Yilmaz said she believed the announcement by Moody's Investors Service that Turkey's sovereign credit ratings might be downgraded because of the deteriorating fiscal position had not taken into account the government's programme for 1997.

She told journalists on Thursday evening she thought Moody's announcement was based solely on Turkey's 1996 economic performance. "There was no statement as to what motives there might be in 1997 to lower the credit rating," she said.

In making an economic evaluation, it was necessary to take into account deviations from targets as a result of the 1994 financial crisis and the problems of trying to form a government in the first seven months of 1996, she said.
She said the Islamist-led government's stability and privatisation programmes planned for 1997 should also be taken into account.
Yilmaz also said the signing of a stand-by agreement between Turkey and the International Monetary Fund (IMF) would depend on resolve by both parties.
Talks with the IMF would continue and a decision on the course of action would follow an IMF committee's visit to Turkey in February, she said.
Some bankers say an IMF deal would strengthen Turkey's ability to borrow abroad in the wake of credit rating downgrades by Standard & Poor's, JCR and IBCA.
